edges.description: Reduced Glrb dosage in mouse models the direction of effect proposed for the human non-coding risk variants.
edges.limitations: The human association is with non-coding regulatory variants producing modest expression differences, whereas the model is a partial gene knockout, so the perturbation is not equivalent in kind or magnitude. Agoraphobia is defined by situational cognitions about escape and help availability, which have no faithful murine counterpart, so the reported agoraphobic phenotype is an avoidance-behavior analogue. The finding is reported as one component of a larger human genetics paper rather than as a dedicated behavioral study.

nodes.description: Fear and avoidance of situations where escape might be difficult or help unavailable, in two or more of the DSM-5 situational clusters.

evidence.reference_title: Agoraphobia: a review of the diagnostic classificatory position and criteria.
evidence.snippet: We come to the conclusion that AG should be conceptualized as an independent disorder with more specific criteria rather than a subordinate, residual form of PD as currently stipulated in DSM-IV-TR.

nodes.description: Catastrophic beliefs that escape would be difficult or help unavailable if incapacitating symptoms occurred. These cognitions are the phenotype on which the GLRB genome-wide association was defined, via the Agoraphobia Cognition Questionnaire.

evidence.reference_title: GLRB allelic variation associated with agoraphobic cognitions, increased startle response and fear network activation: a potential neurogenetic pathway to panic disorder.
evidence.snippet: We therefore performed a genome-wide association study with a dimensional, PD/AG-related anxiety phenotype based on the Agoraphobia Cognition Questionnaire (ACQ) in a sample of 1370 healthy German volunteers of the CRC TRR58 MEGA study wave 1.

nodes.description: Antidepressants are effective for panic disorder with or without agoraphobia and improve agoraphobic avoidance, though the network meta-analytic evidence base is defined on panic disorder populations.

evidence.reference_title: A meta-analysis of the treatment of panic disorder with or without agoraphobia: a comparison of psychopharmacological, cognitive-behavioral, and combination treatments.
evidence.snippet: Antidepressants, psychological panic management, high-potency benzodiazepines, and antidepressants combined with exposure in vivo were superior to the control condition for panic attacks.

nodes.description: Marked anticipatory anxiety about entering or remaining in agoraphobic situations.

evidence.reference_title: The Burden of Agoraphobia in Worsening Quality of Life in a Community Survey in Italy.
evidence.snippet: Current nosology redefined agoraphobia as an autonomous diagnosis distinct from panic disorder.

nodes.description: Carriers of GLRB risk variants show an increased startle reflex and increased fear-network and general sensory activation, an intermediate phenotype linking the genetic finding to the clinical fear response.
nodes.id: Exaggerated Startle and Fear Network Activation

evidence.reference_title: GLRB allelic variation associated with agoraphobic cognitions, increased startle response and fear network activation: a potential neurogenetic pathway to panic disorder.
evidence.snippet: Analyses of intermediate PD/AG phenotypes demonstrated increased startle reflex and increased fear network, as well as general sensory activation by GLRB risk gene variants rs78726293, rs191260602, rs17035816 and rs7688285.

nodes.description: In a meta-analysis of 106 studies of panic disorder with or without agoraphobia, every active treatment examined outperformed control on the agoraphobic avoidance outcome specifically, and the combination of antidepressants with exposure in vivo was superior to all other conditions for that outcome.
nodes.id: Exposure in vivo combined with antidepressant pharmacotherapy

evidence.reference_title: A meta-analysis of the treatment of panic disorder with or without agoraphobia: a comparison of psychopharmacological, cognitive-behavioral, and combination treatments.
evidence.snippet: With regard to agoraphobic avoidance, all seven treatments were superior to the control condition.

evidence.reference_title: A meta-analysis of the treatment of panic disorder with or without agoraphobia: a comparison of psychopharmacological, cognitive-behavioral, and combination treatments.
evidence.snippet: For agoraphobic avoidance, the combination of antidepressants with exposure in vivo was superior to the other conditions.

nodes.description: Non-coding variants in GLRB, encoding the glycine receptor beta subunit, are associated with agoraphobic cognitions at genome-wide significance in a dimensional phenotype based on the Agoraphobia Cognition Questionnaire, and replicate against dichotomous and categorical agoraphobia phenotypes. The same gene carries rare coding mutations causing hyperekplexia, a neurological startle disorder with agoraphobic behavior.

animal_models.description: Reduced Glrb dosage in mouse models the direction of effect proposed for the human non-coding risk variants.
animal_models.name: Partial Glrb knockout mouse

evidence.reference_title: GLRB allelic variation associated with agoraphobic cognitions, increased startle response and fear network activation: a potential neurogenetic pathway to panic disorder.
evidence.snippet: We followed up on this finding in a larger dimensional ACQ sample (N=2547) and in independent samples with a dichotomous AG phenotype based on the Symptoms Checklist (SCL-90; N=3845) and a case-control sample with the categorical phenotype PD/AG (Ncombined =1012) obtaining highly significant P-values also for GLRB single-nucleotide variants rs17035816 (P=3.8 × 10-4) and rs7688285 (P=7.6 × 10-5).

nodes.description: Agoraphobic patients compensate by relying on proprioceptive and visual spatial cues rather than vestibular input for upright balance. On computerized dynamic posturography this shows as surface dependence, impaired balance specifically when proprioceptive information is degraded.

evidence.reference_title: Surface dependence: a balance control strategy in panic disorder with agoraphobia.
evidence.snippet: The agoraphobics had impaired balance when proprioceptive balance information was minimized by sway-referencing the support surface (p < 0.02).

nodes.description: Mice with partial knockout of Glrb, the mouse orthologue of the human agoraphobia-associated gene, were reported to display an agoraphobic behavioral phenotype, supporting the translational relevance of the human genetic association.

evidence.reference_title: GLRB allelic variation associated with agoraphobic cognitions, increased startle response and fear network activation: a potential neurogenetic pathway to panic disorder.
evidence.snippet: Partial Glrb knockout mice demonstrated an agoraphobic phenotype.

nodes.description: The convergent clinical endpoint: fear of, and active avoidance of, the agoraphobic situations. Avoidance is the feature that drives the disorder's course and functional impact, and is the primary target of treatment.

Discomfort in environments providing inadequate or conflicting visual and proprioceptive spatial reference. This is the mechanistic bridge to the specific situational content of agoraphobia, since open spaces, crowds and moving vehicles are exactly the settings in which such cues are degraded.

evidence.reference_title: Space and motion discomfort and abnormal balance control in patients with anxiety disorders.
evidence.snippet: SMD and anxiety responses were independently associated with abnormal balance.

evidence.reference_title: Space and motion discomfort and abnormal balance control in patients with anxiety disorders.
evidence.snippet: In patients with anxiety disorders, higher SMD is indicative of somatosensory dependence in the control of balance.

nodes.description: Peripheral and central vestibular abnormalities are over-represented in agoraphobia and in panic disorder with agoraphobia, and are the proposed initiating lesion of the spatial-orientation strand of the disorder.

evidence.reference_title: Space and motion discomfort and abnormal balance control in patients with anxiety disorders.
evidence.snippet: The presence of either panic attacks or fear of heights increased the probability of having caloric hypofunction in a non-additive fashion.
